analysis:
Documentation-only PR. docs/provider/troubleshooting.md: the date bump (line 3) and line 140 now cite CoordinatorReconnectPolicy and CoordinatorReconnectPolicy.swift instead of ExponentialBackoff in CoordinatorClient+Connection.swift. docs/reference/protocol-messages.md: adds a new "Close codes and the reconnect wait" section (head lines 198-215) describing that the provider reads only the WebSocket close code and not the reason. Code 1012 gives a wait drawn from serviceRestartDelayRange without growing the backoff. Any other code, or no close frame, gives the next ExponentialBackoff range and the backoff grows. A session open for stableSessionDuration or more, counted from register, resets the backoff. Every reconnect sends a fresh register.

No source, control or wire-format change is visible in the supplied evidence. The security-relevant claims are the 1012 handling and the fresh register per reconnect. Fresh register is consistent with the existing per-socket nonce and endpoint-resumption design (T-053, TB-002). A 1012 short delay lets a coordinator-side actor shorten reconnect waits. The coordinator is trusted, and the provider reads only the code, which is bounded by serviceRestartDelayRange. The backoff is not grown, so a hostile or buggy coordinator could in theory cause fast reconnect loops. That is a coordinator-trusted, availability-only matter and not a regression shown by this docs change.

Unverified contract: the actual implementation in CoordinatorReconnectPolicy.swift and the values of serviceRestartDelayRange and stableSessionDuration are not supplied. The reviewer cannot confirm that the documentation matches the code, or that the 1012 range is bounded appropriately, so the next pass should check the code if available. No threat-model assumption is invalidated and no new attack surface is introduced by the docs.
